title: Get the health probe's request past the load balancer

blocks.text: The health checker probes each service over a plain socket and writes its HTTP/1.1 request by hand. On a developer's Windows laptop the probes pass. On the Linux monitoring host the load balancer answers every one of them with `400 Bad Request`, and the service behind it never sees the request.
`HealthProbe.send` already writes the request head to the socket. Build that head in the `TODO` of `src/main/java/practice/HealthProbe.java`: `head(host, path, accept)` returns
where every line, the empty last one included, ends with a carriage return and a line feed, as HTTP/1.1 requires.
When you're done, the probe sends the same bytes from Linux and from Windows, and a strict server reads three lines and an empty one. About four lines in total.

cases.says: the request sent to the socket is a GET that names the path, the host and the accepted type
every line of the request ends with CR LF, whatever machine the probe runs on, and the head ends with an empty line
the request line, the Host header and the Accept header are separate lines, followed by an empty one
the request line separates the method, the path and the version with single spaces

origin.section: `\n` Is Always a Line Feed; `%n`, `println` and `lineSeparator()` Follow the Platform

concepts: \n is a single line feed on every platform, while %n, println and System.lineSeparator() write the line.separator the JVM started with, so a format with fixed line endings needs the escape it requires.

A value built from literals joined with + holds only what is between the quotes, so a missing line break or space at a seam joins two lines or two words, and a SQL -- comment then swallows the rest of the statement.
